tips.text: Taegeuk refers to the source of everything in the universe and the universal law in which everything continuously goes through cycles of creation and destruction.
Pumse Taegeuk symbolizes the root principle of universal philosophy and is constructed by applying the truth inherent in Taegeuk's yin and yang principles.
Taegeuk Ojang stands for song of the eight trigrams and symbolizes calm and authority.
Taegeuk Ojang is a pumse that emphasizes techniques of self-defense rather than athletic function.
We will now take a look at the pumse of Taegeuk Ojang.

These are the key moves of Taegeuk Ojang.
We will now take a closer look at each of the key moves of Taegeuk Ojang.
Mejumok Neryochigi is a technique used to strike an opponent by drawing a big descending circle with your hammer fist.
While your arms cross at the solar plexus, your assisting arm should face outward.
The striking hand should pass under the assisting arm.
Draw an arc above your head and stop at the shoulder line with your arm naturally straightened.
Your fist should not stop at the head.

Palgunji Neryochigi is a technique used to strike with the elbow in a swinging motion.
Bend your elbow so the back of your hand faces upward.
Place the fist in front of the shoulder of your striking arm.
Spin your torso and strike.
The elbow should be slightly above your shoulder.
Your chest should open up when performing the move.

Goasogi is a posture where you bend your knees by twisting your feet using a low stance one fist's width between your feet.
Stand low like Juchumsogi with the shin of one leg touching the calf of the other.
Apgoasogi refers to moving sideways and performing Goasogi in front of the supporting leg,
while Duigoasogi refers to placing the other foot behind the forward foot to perform Goasogi, then coming to a halt.

Yopsogi is a posture where you twist one foot 90 degrees outward from the Naranhisogi posture.
Straighten your knees and stand naturally with one foot's length between your feet.
Your center should be between your feet.
These are the key moves of Taeguk-Ojang.
We will now look at the moves in succession, connecting each move.
The key moves of Taeguk-Ojang first part consist of
Wen Aremaki, Wen Mejumok Neryeochigi, Orun Aremaki, and Orun Mejumok Neryeochigi.
Push off the ground with your front foot from Apgubi Aremaki.
Move your center to your hind leg.
Stand in Yopsogi posture, then perform Mejumok Neryeochigi.
All must be performed in one continuous motion.
Your eyes should follow the direction of Pumsae.
Cautions for Taeguk-Ojang first part, taking a closer look.
Do not perform Mejumok Neryeochigi in a similar fashion to Doongjungmok Pakachigi,
and your first should not pass in front of your face when striking.
We will now practice the moves of Taeguk-Ojang first part in succession while watching the video.
The key moves of Taeguk-Ojang second part consist of
Wen Anmaki, and Orun Anmaki, Orun Apchagi, and Orun Doongjungmok Apchigi, and Wen Anmaki.
Breathe in after performing Wen Makki, then connect to Orun Makki.
Bend your knee using the momentum from Apchagi, then perform the preparatory Doongjungmok Apchigi move.
After the kicking foot touches ground, connect the Doongjungmok Apchigi and Anmaki.
Concentrate on the use of your breath and muscles and coordinate spinning of the torso while connecting the moves.
Cautions for Taeguk-Ojang second part, taking a closer look.
Connect the moves so the Wen Anmaki and Orun Anmaki flow naturally.
The target for Doongjungmok Apchigi is above the philtrum.
Be careful not to let your fist rise above your shoulder when performing Anmaki.
The key moves of Taeguk-Ojang third part consist of
Wen Solnal Pakkatmaki, Orun Palkumchi Doryochigi, Orun Solnal Pakkatmaki, Wen Palkumchi Doryochigi, Wen Aremaki, and Orun Anmaki, Orun Apchagi, and Orun Aremaki, and Wen Anmaki.
Then connect Aremaki and Anmaki when the kicking foot touches the ground.
Cautions for Taeguk-Ojang third part, taking a closer look.
Apchagi and Anmaki, Anmaki moves should all be performed in succession.
When performing Palkumchi Doryochigi, the targeting hand should not wrap around the elbow.
The key moves of Taeguk-Ojang fourth part consist of

Wen Olgulmaki, Orun Yeopchagi, and Wen Palkumchi Pyojokchigi, Orun Olgulmaki, Wen Yeopchagi, and Orun Palkumchi Pyojokchigi, Wen Aremaki, and Orun Anmaki, and Orun Apchagi, and Orun Ddeungjumok Apchigi.

Yeopchagi and the movement of both arms should be performed simultaneously.
Twist your torso about 45 degrees and strike a target at solar plexus elevation with your elbow.
Arm and hand movements should be performed simultaneously.
When performing Apchagi and Ddeungjumok Apchigi,
the foot blade of the striking foot should maintain a 45 degree angle when seen from the front.
Complete the move by performing Ddeungjumok Apchigi the moment the following foot touches the ground.
This concludes the training for Taeguk Ojang.
We will take another look at all the moves and master Pumse.
We have looked at the key moves of Taeguk Ojang
and provided thorough explanations for each move and things to watch out for.
You will be able to hone even more accurate and delicate moves
